steps.context: User-reported mid-batch (2026-09-18): the daily scraper cron re-requests an overlapping date window every run instead of scraping incrementally. Root cause: scraper.ts's EventBridge daily-batch path hardcodes `newerThan = now - 7 days` for every account on every invocation (~6-day overlap with the previous day's window, forever -- real recurring Bright Data/Apify metered vendor cost, not AWS free-tier float). The correct incremental logic already exists in process-scrape-job.ts:132-139 (use newestPost.publishedAt from `SELECT publishedAt FROM posts WHERE accountId=... ORDER BY publishedAt DESC LIMIT 1`, falling back to env.scrapeInitialLookbackDays only when the account has zero posts yet) but is only wired into the SQS-fallback path, never the primary async-trigger path that drives the cron. Fix: extend getBatchScrapeTargets() (apps/backend/src/lib/scraper/get-scrape-targets.ts) with a MAX(publishedAt) GROUP BY accountId join against posts (single batched query, not N+1 per target), attach it to ScrapeTarget, then replace scraper.ts:91's hardcoded window with `target.newestPostPublishedAt?.toISOString() ?? lookbackFallback(env.scrapeInitialLookbackDays)`. Reuses an already-proven pattern from this same codebase -- no new mechanism, no architectural/UX ambiguity. Full evidence: backlog/FIND-035-scraper-batch-non-incremental-window.md. Prioritized ahead of FIND-024/FIND-022/IDEA-010 per user direction (low-risk, high-value).
